parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description:
The data format processed by the rule. This value must match the data format of the device data to be processed. Valid values:

- **JSON** (default): JSON data.
- **BINARY**: binary data.

> If you set this parameter to **BINARY**, **TopicType** cannot be set to 0 (basic communication topic or Thing Specification Language model communication topic), and data forwarding to <props="china"><ph>time series data storage within the instance, time series databases, </ph></props>Tablestore or ApsaraDB RDS is not supported.

parameters.name: IotInstanceId
parameters.description:
The instance ID. On the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console, you can view the **ID** of the current instance.

><notice>
- If this parameter has a value, you must specify this parameter. Otherwise, the call fails.
- If no **Overview** page exists or no ID value is available, you do not need to specify this parameter.

></notice>

For more information about instances, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: The rule name. The name can contain Chinese characters, letters, Japanese characters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length. A Chinese character or Japanese character counts as 2 characters.

parameters.name: ProductKey
parameters.description: The ProductKey of the product to which the rule applies.

parameters.name: ResourceGroupId
parameters.description:
The resource group ID.

><notice>
- Currently, IoT Platform supports resource group management only at the instance level. The request parameter **ResourceGroupId** is no longer valid and does not need to be specified.
- Resource groups previously set by calling this operation remain effective.

></notice>

parameters.name: RuleDesc
parameters.description: The description of the rule. The description can be up to 100 characters in length. A Chinese character counts as 1 character.

parameters.name: Select
parameters.description:
The SQL SELECT statement to execute. For more information, see [SQL expressions](~~30554~~).

> Specify only the content after SELECT. For example, if the SELECT statement is `SELECT a,b,c`, specify `a,b,c`.

parameters.name: ShortTopic
parameters.description:
The specific topic to which the rule applies. The format is generally: `${deviceName}/topicShortName`. `${deviceName}` is the name of the specific device, and `topicShortName` is the short name of the topic.

- For basic communication topics or Thing Specification Language model communication topics, the ShortTopic format is generally: `${deviceName}/topicShortName`. `${deviceName}` can be replaced with the wildcard `+` to represent all device names under the product. Valid values of `topicShortName`:

    - `/thing/event/property/post`: property messages reported by devices.
    - `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: event messages reported by devices. The value in `${}` is the event identifier in the Thing Specification Language model of the product.
    - `/thing/lifecycle`: device lifecycle change messages.
    - `/thing/downlink/reply/message`: result messages of device responses to cloud commands.
    - `/thing/list/found`: messages reported by gateways about discovered sub-devices.
    - `/thing/topo/lifecycle`: device topology relationship change messages.
    - `/thing/event/property/history/post`: historical property messages reported by devices.
    - `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/history/post`: historical event messages reported by devices. The value in `${}` is the event identifier in the Thing Specification Language model of the product.
    - `/ota/upgrade`: device OTA update status notification messages.
    - `/ota/version/post`: device OTA module version number reporting messages.
    - `/thing/deviceinfo/update`: device tag change messages.
    - `/edge/driver/${driver_id}/point_post`: pass-through mode topic messages of IoT Edge. The value in `${}` is the device access driver ID of IoT Edge.

 The OTA update batch status notification topic also belongs to basic communication topics. The ShortTopic format is: `${packageId}/${jobId}/ota/job/status`. `${packageId}` is over-the-air update package ID, and `${jobId}` is over-the-air update batch ID.
- For custom topics, the ShortTopic format is, for example: `${deviceName}/user/get`.

  Call the [QueryProductTopic](~~69647~~) operation to view all custom topic categories under the product.

    When specifying a custom topic, you can use the wildcards `+` and `#`.
    - `${deviceName}` can be replaced with the wildcard `+` to represent all devices under the product.
    - Subsequent fields can use `/user/#`, where `#` represents all level names after the `/user` level.
    For more information about using wildcards, see [Wildcards in topic categories](~~85539~~).
- The ShortTopic for device status change notification topics: `${deviceName}`.

 You can directly use the wildcard `+` to represent status change notifications for all devices under the product.

parameters.name: Topic
parameters.description:
The complete topic to which to add a rule.

If you specify this parameter, you do not need to specify **ShortTopic** or **TopicType**.

parameters.name: TopicType
parameters.description:
- **0**: a basic communication topic or Thing Specification Language model communication topic as described in the **ShortTopic** parameter, including the OTA upgrade batch status notification topic.
- **1**: a custom topic.
- **2**: a device status change notification topic: `/as/mqtt/status/${productKey}/${deviceName}`.

parameters.name: Where
parameters.description:
The trigger condition of the rule. For more information, see [SQL expressions](~~30554~~).

> Specify only the content in **Where**. For example, if the **Where** statement is `Where a>10`, specify `a>10`.
